title: The sync that did not wait

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where the demo runs the evening sync against a healthy store and a failing one.

tasks.title: Catch the sync returning early
tasks.description:
Before you change anything, measure the bug. In `src/reproduce.js`, implement `async reproduceEarlyReturn()`.

Make a store with `createFakeStore()` and `await` the original `syncBookings(evening, store)`. Return an object with:

- `returned`: what `syncBookings` resolved with
- `savedWhenReturned`: `store.saved().length` right after that `await`
- `savedLater`: `store.saved().length` after you wait another 100 ms

The check runs your function against the original `sync.js`.
nextSteps: Run `node src/demo.js` and compare the count with what the store holds.
Wait 100 ms with a promise around `setTimeout`, then read it again.
Return all three numbers and run the demo again.
hints: `await` waits for the promise `syncBookings` returns, and nothing else. What does that promise wait for?
`await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 100))` pauses an async function for 100 ms.
With the original code you should see 3 returned, 0 saved when it returned and 3 saved later.

tasks.title: Wait for every save
tasks.description:
Fix `syncBookings(bookings, store)` in `src/sync.js`.

- It calls `store.save(booking)` for every booking.
- It resolves with the number of bookings, only after every save has finished.
- If a save fails, it rejects with that error, so `await syncBookings(...)` inside a `try...catch` catches it. No error may escape as an unhandled rejection.
- An empty list resolves with `0`.

Saving one after another or all at once are both fine. The check runs your function against fake stores, some with a failing save.
nextSteps: Find what `forEach` does with the promises your callback returns.
Choose: a `for...of` loop with `await`, or `Promise.all` over the saves.
Make sure the function only returns after that waiting is done.
Run `node src/demo.js` and check both lines.
hints: An async callback returns a promise. `forEach` calls it and throws that promise away, so nobody waits for it and nobody catches its error.
Putting `await` in front of `forEach` does nothing: `forEach` returns `undefined`, and awaiting `undefined` finishes at once.
Either await each save inside a `for...of` loop, or turn the bookings into an array of save promises with `map` and await `Promise.all` of it.

tasks.title: Write the test that would have caught it
tasks.description:
Write vitest tests in `src/sync.test.js` with stores from `createFakeStore`. They should check that:

- as soon as `syncBookings` resolves, every booking is in `store.saved()`
- when a save fails (use `failOn`), `syncBookings` rejects with an error that names the booking

Keep them fast with a small `delayMs`. The check runs your test file three times: beside the original `sync.js` (it must fail), beside a correct fix (it must pass) and beside a fix that puts `await` in front of `forEach` (it must fail).
nextSteps: Write a test that awaits `syncBookings` and then reads `store.saved()`.
Write a test with `failOn` that expects the promise to reject.
Run `npx vitest run src/sync.test.js` against your fixed code.
Ask yourself why the await forEach fix fails your first test.
hints: Read the store immediately after the `await`. Waiting longer in a test would hide the bug.
`await expect(promise).rejects.toThrow('Could not save b102')` checks a rejection.
Sort `store.saved()` before comparing if your fix may save in parallel, so the test does not depend on finishing order.
